source.text: ወእምህየ፡ ሖርኩ፡ መንገለ፡ አዜብ፡ በአጽናፈ፡ ምድር፡ ወበህየ፡ ርኢኩ፡ *ሠለስተ፡ ኆዋኅወ፡ ሰማይ፡ ርኁዋተ፡ ወይወፅእ፡ እምህየ፡ †አዜብ፡† ወጠል፡ ወዝናም፡ ወነፋስ።
source.note: Fresh bounded collation of actual Charles 1906 scan. Critical marks retained in source.text and source_diplomatic; edition is not an independent manuscript witness.

translation.text: From there I went south to the ends of the earth. There I saw three open portals of heaven, and from there come the south[a], dew, rain, and wind.

footnotes.text: The printed edition marks “south” as corrupt here. Charles suggests that the underlying wording may have concerned moisture, or that “south” may have entered as a marginal explanation of “from there.” This translation retains the printed word rather than silently adopting either conjecture.

source.text: ወእምህየ፡ ሖርኩ፡ መንገለ፡ ጽባሕ፡ በአጽናፈ፡ ሰማይ፡ ወ*በህየ፡ ርኢኩ፡ ሠለስተ፡ ኆዋኅወ፡ ሰማይ፡ ርኁዋተ፡ መንገለ፡ ጽባሕ፡ ወላዕሌሆሙ፡ ኆዋኅወ፡ ንኡሳነ።
source.note: Fresh bounded collation of actual Charles 1906 scan. Critical marks retained in source.text and source_diplomatic; edition is not an independent manuscript witness.

translation.text: From there I went east to the ends of heaven. There I saw three open portals of heaven toward the east, and above them small portals.

source.text: በበ፩፡ እምእሌክ፡ ኆዋኅወ፡ ንኡሳነ፡ የሐልፉ፡ ከዋክብተ፡ ሰማይ፡ ወየሐውሩ፡ *ምዕራበ፡ በፍኖት፡ እንተ፡ ተርእየት፡ ሎሙ።
source.note: Fresh bounded collation of actual Charles 1906 scan. Critical marks retained in source.text and source_diplomatic; edition is not an independent manuscript witness.

translation.text: Through each of these small portals the stars of heaven pass, and they travel west along the path shown to them.

source.text: ወሶበ፡ ርኢኩ፡ ባረኩ፡ በኵሉ፡ ጊዜ፡ ወእባርኮ፡ ለ*እግዚአ፡ ስብሐት፡ ዘገብረ፡ ተአምራተ፡ ዓቢያነ፡ ወስቡሓነ፡ ከመ፡ ያርኢ፡ ዕበየ፡ ግብሩ፡ ለመላእክቲሁ፡ ወ*ለነፍሳት፡ ወለሰብእ፡ ከመ፡ ይስብሕዎ፡ ግብሮ፡ *ወኵሎ፡ ተግባሮ፡ ከመ፡ ይርአዩ፡ *ግብረ፡ ኃይሉ፡ ወ*ይስብሕዎ፡ ለግብረ፡ እዴሁ፡ ዓቢይ፡ ወይባርክዎ፡ እስከ፡ ለዓለም።
source.note: Fresh bounded collation of actual Charles 1906 scan. Critical marks retained in source.text and source_diplomatic; edition is not an independent manuscript witness.

translation.text: When I saw this, I blessed, and at all times I bless the Lord of Glory, who has done great and glorious wonders to show the greatness of his work to his angels, to spirits, and to humankind[a], so that they might praise his work and all his deeds, that they might see the work of his power and praise the great work of his hands and bless him forever.

footnotes.text: The selected edition prints “to spirits, and to humankind.” Its apparatus records other readings including “to the spirits of humankind.” These are variants reported by the editor, not independently inspected manuscripts.

source.text: *ራእይ፡ ዘርእየ፡ ካልእ፡ ራእየ፡ ጥበብ፡ ዘርእየ፡ ሄኖክ፡ ወልደ፡ ያሬድ፡ ወልደ፡ መላልኤል፡ ወልደ፡ ቃይናን፡ ወልደ፡ ሄኖስ፡ ወልደ፡ ሴት፡ ወልደ፡ አዳም።
source.note: Fresh bounded collation of actual Charles 1906 scan. Critical marks retained in source.text and source_diplomatic; edition is not an independent manuscript witness.

translation.text: A vision that he saw: a second vision of wisdom that Enoch, son of Jared, son of Mahalalel, son of Cainan, son of Enos, son of Seth, son of Adam, saw.[a]

footnotes.text: The printed heading repeats “vision” and “saw”; this translation retains the repetition. “Second” can also be rendered “another.” The apparatus records differing omissions in the heading.

source.text: ወዝ፡ ርእሱ፡ ለነገረ፡ ጥበብ፡ ዘ*አንሣእኩ፡ እትናገር፡ [እብል፡] ለእለ፡ የኃድሩ፡ ውስተ፡ የብስ፡ ስምዑ፡ ቀደምት፡ ወርእዩ፡ ደኃርያን፡ ነገረ፡ ቅዱሰ፡ እለ፡ እትናገር፡ ቅድመ፡ እግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት።
source.note: Fresh bounded collation of actual Charles 1906 scan. Critical marks retained in source.text and source_diplomatic; edition is not an independent manuscript witness.

translation.text: This is the beginning of the word of wisdom that I have taken up to speak[a] to those who dwell on dry land: “Hear, you former ones, and see, you latter ones[b], the holy words that I speak before the Lord of Spirits.”

footnotes.text: The edition brackets እብል, “I say,” as a duplicated expression. It is recorded in the source but is not translated as a second speaking clause.
The address distinguishes former and latter people, naturally understood as earlier and later generations; the translation preserves the temporal contrast.

source.text: እሉ፡ ቀዳሚ፡ ይኄይስ፡ ብሂል፡ ወ*ደኃርያንሂ፡ ኢንከልእ፡ ርእሳ፡ ለጥበብ።
source.note: Fresh bounded collation of actual Charles 1906 scan. Critical marks retained in source.text and source_diplomatic; edition is not an independent manuscript witness.

translation.text: It is better to speak to these former ones[a], but we will not withhold the beginning of wisdom from the latter ones either.

footnotes.text: The opening “these former ones” stands apart grammatically in the printed Ge’ez. This translation connects it with “to speak”; the editor records alternative case forms.

source.text: እስከ፡ ይእዜ፡ ኢተውህበኒ፡ እምቅድመ፡ እግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት፡ ዘነሣእኩ፡ ጥበብ፡ በከመ፡ ኃለይኩ፡ በከመ፡ ፈቀደ፡ እግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት፡ ዘተውህበኒ፡ እምኔሁ፡ ክፍለ፡ ሕይወት፡ ዘለዓለም።
source.note: Fresh bounded collation of actual Charles 1906 scan. Critical marks retained in source.text and source_diplomatic; edition is not an independent manuscript witness.

translation.text: Until now, the wisdom I have received had not been given to me from the presence of the Lord of Spirits, as I considered, as the Lord of Spirits willed, from whom a share of eternal life was given to me.[a]

footnotes.text: The syntax of this statement is difficult. The selected edition prints a negative at its opening and repeats “as”; the rendering preserves these rather than supplying an unexpressed comparison such as “greater wisdom.” Its apparatus records a manuscript reading “which” in place of the negative. The final clauses continue across the page and explicitly mention wisdom and a share of eternal life.

source.text: ወኮኑ፡ ብየ፡ ሠለስቱ፡ ምሳሌ፡ ወአነ፡ አንሣእኩ፡ እንዘ፡ እብሎሙ፡ ለእለ፡ *የኃድሩ፡ ዲበ፡ የብስ።
source.note: Fresh bounded collation of actual Charles 1906 scan. Critical marks retained in source.text and source_diplomatic; edition is not an independent manuscript witness.

translation.text: Three parables came to me[a], and I took them up, telling them to those who dwell on dry land.

footnotes.text: More literally, “there were three parables with me.”
